s.es: busca líneas que coinciden con un patrón (texto o expresión regular)

syn: grep [OPTION]... PATTERNS [FILE]... ⏎ grep [OPTION]... -e PATTERNS ... [FILE]... ⏎ grep [OPTION]... -f PATTERN_FILE ... [FILE]...

p.es: Lo que se busca: texto o expresión regular. Si tiene espacios o símbolos, ponlo entre comillas.
p.en: What to search for: text or regular expression. If it contains spaces or symbols, quote it.

p.es: Archivo(s) donde buscar. Sin archivos lee la entrada estándar (con -r, el directorio actual).
p.en: File(s) to search. With none reads standard input (with -r, the current directory).

tip: Comillas simples para el patrón: «grep 'a.*b'» evita que la shell interprete * ? $ antes que grep.

o.es: No distingue mayúsculas de minúsculas.
o.en: Ignore case distinctions.

o.es: Invierte: muestra las líneas que NO coinciden.
o.en: Invert the sense of matching: show non-matching lines.

o.es: Busca recursivamente en un directorio (sin seguir enlaces simbólicos).
o.en: Read all files under each directory, recursively (without following symlinks).

o.es: Como -r pero siguiendo enlaces simbólicos.
o.en: Like -r but following all symlinks.

o.es: Muestra el número de línea de cada coincidencia.
o.en: Prefix each line of output with its line number.

o.es: Muestra solo los nombres de archivo que contienen coincidencias.
o.en: Print only the names of files containing matches.

o.es: Muestra los archivos SIN coincidencias.
o.en: Print the names of files with no matches.

o.es: Cuenta las líneas que coinciden en vez de mostrarlas.
o.en: Print a count of matching lines.

o.es: Muestra solo la parte que coincide, no toda la línea.
o.en: Print only the matched parts of a line.

o.es: La coincidencia debe ser una palabra completa.
o.en: Match only whole words.

o.es: La coincidencia debe ocupar la línea entera.
o.en: Match only whole lines.

o.es: Expresiones regulares extendidas (permiten + ? | () {} sin barra invertida).
o.en: Extended regular expressions (allow + ? | () {} without backslash).

o.es: Busca texto literal, sin interpretar caracteres especiales (más rápido).
o.en: Search literal text, no special characters (faster).

o.es: Expresiones regulares estilo Perl (\d, \w, lookahead…).
o.en: Perl-style regular expressions (\d, \w, lookahead…).

o.es: Usa PATRÓN como patrón; sirve para varios patrones o uno que empiece por «-».
o.en: Use PATTERN as pattern; for several patterns or one starting with "-".

o.es: Lee los patrones de un archivo, uno por línea.
o.en: Take patterns from a file, one per line.

o.es: Muestra NUM líneas DESPUÉS de cada coincidencia.
o.en: Print NUM lines of trailing context.

o.es: Muestra NUM líneas ANTES de cada coincidencia.
o.en: Print NUM lines of leading context.

o.es: Muestra NUM líneas antes y después.
o.en: Print NUM lines of output context.

o.es: No muestra el nombre del archivo en cada línea.
o.en: Suppress the prefixing of file names on output.

o.es: Muestra siempre el nombre del archivo.
o.en: Print the file name for each match.

o.es: Suprime los errores de archivos inexistentes o ilegibles.
o.en: Suppress error messages about nonexistent or unreadable files.

o.es: No escribe nada: solo el código de salida (0 = hubo coincidencia).
o.en: Quiet: write nothing, exit with 0 if a match was found.

o.es: Se detiene tras NUM líneas coincidentes.
o.en: Stop reading a file after NUM matching lines.

o.es: Trata los archivos binarios como texto.
o.en: Process a binary file as if it were text.

o.es: Ignora los archivos binarios.
o.en: Process a binary file as if it did not contain matching data.

o.es: Con -r, busca solo en archivos cuyo nombre coincida (p. ej. "*.log").
o.en: With -r, search only files whose name matches (e.g. "*.log").

o.es: Con -r, omite los archivos que coincidan.
o.en: With -r, skip files whose name matches.

o.es: Con -r, omite los directorios que coincidan.
o.en: With -r, skip directories that match.

o.es: Resalta las coincidencias (always, auto, never).
o.en: Surround the matched strings with colour markers.

o.es: Las «líneas» terminan en byte nulo.
o.en: Treat input and output data as sequences of lines terminated by a zero byte.
Output a usage message and exit.
Output the version number of grep and exit.
Interpret PATTERNS as basic regular expressions (BREs, see below). This is the default.

Do not ignore case distinctions in patterns and input data. This is the default. This option is useful for passing to shell scripts that already use -i, to cancel its effects because the two options override each other.
Print the 0-based byte offset within the input file before each line of output. If -o (--only-matching) is specified, print the offset of the matching part itself.

Display input actually coming from standard input as input coming from file LABEL. This can be useful for commands that transform a file's contents before searching, e.g., gzip -cd foo.gz | grep --label=foo -H 'some pattern'. See also the -H option.

Make sure that the first character of actual line content lies on a tab stop, so that the alignment of tabs looks normal. This is useful with options that prefix their output to the actual content: -H,-n, and -b.

Output a zero byte (the ASCII NUL character) instead of the character that normally follows a file name. For example, grep -lZ outputs a zero byte after each file name instead of the usual newline. This option makes the output unambiguous, even in the presence of file names containing unusual characters like newlines.
When -A, -B, or -C are in use, print SEP instead of -- between groups of lines.
When -A, -B, or -C are in use, do not print a separator between groups of lines.

If a file's data or metadata indicate that the file contains binary data, assume that the file is of type TYPE. Non-text bytes indicate binary data; these are either output bytes that are improperly encoded for the current locale, or null input bytes when the -z option is not given.

If an input file is a device, FIFO or socket, use ACTION to process it. By default, ACTION is read, which means that devices are read just as if they were ordinary files. If ACTION is skip, devices are silently skipped.

If an input file is a directory, use ACTION to process it. By default, ACTION is read, i.e., read directories just as if they were ordinary files. If ACTION is skip, silently skip directories. If ACTION is recurse, read all files under each directory, recursively, following symbolic links only if they are on the command line.
Skip files whose base name matches any of the file-name globs read from FILE (using wildcard matching as described under --exclude).
Use line buffering on output. This can cause a performance penalty.

Treat the file(s) as binary. By default, under MS-DOS and MS-Windows, grep guesses whether a file is text or binary as described for the --binary-files option. If grep decides the file is a text file, it strips the CR characters from the original file contents (to make regular expressions with ^ and $ work correctly).
